title: Remark
body_md:
Common choices of $ {\mathcal B} $ include the unit ball $ {\mathcal B}^n $, the unit cube $ [-1,1]^n $, the fundamental Voronoi region $ {\mathcal V}_\Lambda $ of a (full-rank) lattice $ \Lambda\subset{\mathbb R}^n $, etc. 
Some choices of ${\mathcal B}$ may be more convenient than the others for analyzing certain ensembles of packings. 
Therefore, we do not fix the choice of ${\mathcal B}$ in \Cref{def:packing-euclidean}.

The rate of a packing (as per \Cref{eqn:density-unbounded}) is also called the \emph{normalized logarithmic density} in the literature. 
It measures the the normalized number of points per unit volume.

label: def:cheb-rad-avg-rad
title: Definition
head: environment
name: Chebyshev radius and average squared radius of a list

title: Remark
body_md:
One should note that for an $L$-list ${\mathcal L}$ of points, the smallest ball containing ${\mathcal L}$ is not necessarily the same as the \emph{circumscribed ball}, i.e., the ball such that all points in ${\mathcal L}$ live on the boundary of the ball. 
The circumscribed ball of the polytope $ \operatorname{conv}\mleft\{{\mathcal L}\mright\} $ spanned by the points in ${\mathcal L}$ may not exist. 
If it does exist, it is not necessarily the smallest one containing $ {\mathcal L} $. 
However, whenever it exists, the smallest ball containing ${\mathcal L}$ must be the circumscribed ball of a certain \emph{subset} of ${\mathcal L}$.

label: thm:two-notions-unbdd-density
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:two-notions-unbdd-density}
Let $ N>0 $ and $ L\in{\mathbb Z}_{\ge2} $. 
Let $ {\mathcal C}\subset{\mathbb R}^n $ be an $(N,L-1)$-multiple packing. 
Then $ \Delta({\mathcal C}) \stackrel{n\to\infty}{\asymp} R({\mathcal C}) + \frac{1}{2}\ln(2\pi eN) $.

title: Remark
body_md:
Note that the above bound (\Cref{eqn:lb-ppp}) approaches $ \frac{1}{2}\ln\frac{1}{2\pi eN} $ as $ L\to\infty $. 
The latter quantity is known to be the list-decoding capacity for asymptotically large $L$ (see \Cref{sec:listdec-cap-large}). 
On the extreme, when $L=2$, the above bound becomes $ \frac{1}{2}\ln\frac{1}{8\pi eN} $ which recovers the best known bound due to Minkowski \cite{minkowski-sphere-pack}.

label: lemma:finitecodebook_avgrad
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:finitecodebook_avgrad}
  There exists a finite codebook ${\mathcal C}_K$ supported over ${\mathcal A}$, having minimum average squared radius at least $\sqrt{nN}$ and density
  \[
    \frac{1}{n}\ln \frac{|{\mathcal C}_K|}{|{\mathcal A}|} \geq \frac{1}{2}\ln\frac{L-1}{2\pi eNL} - \frac{1}{2(L-1)}\ln L +o(1).
  \]
head: environment

label: lemma:avg_rad_exponent
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:avg_rad_exponent}
  For any ${\underline{\mathbf{x}}}_1,\cdots,{\underline{\mathbf{x}}}_L$ drawn independently and uniformly at random from ${\mathcal A}$, we have
  \[
    \Pr\mleft[\overline\operatorname{rad}^2({\underline{\mathbf{x}}}_1,\cdots,{\underline{\mathbf{x}}}_L) \le nN\mright] = e^{nE(K)+o(n)} ,
  \]
  where the $o(n)$ term is independent of $K$, and
  \[
E(K)\coloneqq \frac{L-1}{2}\ln\frac{L-1}{2\pi eNL} - \frac{1}{2}\ln L + (L-1)\ln (2K). 
  \]
head: environment
